protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 2 of 3; refute not confirm; one owner-recording entry for DR-004 under adopted D-054 / D-057
summary: The subject moved during this review and so did the review prompt. I measured 4a28b6fc three times at start, matching the dispatch; it now measures 28719de6, stable across four measurements a second apart, 102 lines, mtime 11:51, untracked and not written by me. The prompt went from 1919f0af to 12a5c44d. The dispatch said the subject is frozen and to OBJECT if it moves, so I do. On the bytes I actually read the substance is clean: my C2-D059-01 repair landed, with COORD re-measured to 658c4d15 matching live, and all eight cited digests and four commits verify. One note records the only thing lost in that repair — the 21f0945 commit reference for D-058's adoption, which I had specifically credited at turn 1.

objections.location: the subject file itself, and the review prompt
objections.claim: The subject did not stay frozen for the duration of the review, and the dispatch instruction itself changed under it. The bytes I reviewed are not the current bytes, and no independent review exists for the current ones.
evidence: The dispatch pins 4a28b6fc9853d4474af9de63f4c3fd77584ca25238d51d7b2d7bf02744920d58 and states 'This subject is FROZEN. If it moves, OBJECT.' I reproduced that digest three times at start.

The subject now measures 28719de662a2ccd2a0da289e78a554606a7e7623a37ae262b4bc1788d32543ea, identical across four consecutive measurements taken a second apart, so it is stable rather than mid-write. It is 102 lines, 4510 bytes, mtime Aug 14 11:51.
The review prompt also moved, from 1919f0af9ba5dfe696b9e2ce0577e01e9a1d83522ebe1d7dc238b7325e170aad at my start to 12a5c44d1aa665d6aa9b8caef29828985bc02e83d8feabb1e97fcb2e60269290.
Neither is mine: both are untracked working-tree files, my filesEdited is empty, and git reports zero modified tracked files.
objections.whyItIsABlocker: This corpus adopts digests. An adopted D-059 citing this verdict against 4a28b6fc would record a review of bytes that no longer exist; citing it against 28719de6 would attribute to me a review I did not perform. The start-and-end measurement exists precisely to catch this, and the dispatch made the consequence explicit.
objections.remedy: Re-dispatch at the digest of the bytes actually under review, and hold both the subject and the prompt for the duration of the cycle.
objections.patternWorthNaming: The freeze control had been working. Counting this family: D-054 turn 1 moved during review; D-057 turn 1 never matched its dispatch; D-057 turn 2 moved and its prompt moved; then six consecutive dispatches held — D-057 turn 3, D-058/D-059, D-059-063, D-058.owner, D-058, and D-059 turn 1. This is the first failure since that run, and it is the second time the prompt has moved alongside the subject. The gap is not the review window, which is now well controlled, but the practice of continuing to edit a dispatched artifact after dispatch.

notesRecorded.location: the 'Own cycle' sentence, in the bytes I reviewed
notesRecorded.observation: The repair dropped a verifiable reference while fixing an unrelated one. Turn 1 read 'Own cycle. D-058 already adopted at `21f0945` for DR-002.' The reviewed turn-2 bytes read 'Own cycle. D-058 already adopted for DR-002.' A token-loss pass returns exactly three tokens: the stale COORD digest 6f5557df, which is the repair itself; 'at'; and '21f0945'.
notesRecorded.whyItIsOnlyANote: D-058 is a sibling owner recording for a different row, not a dependency of D-059, so its adoption commit is not one of D-057's required pins. The remaining claim is also true: live COORD contains exactly one '## D-058' heading, titled 'Owner-record the DR-002 preview Route B disposition'. Nothing false is asserted and no required pin is missing.
notesRecorded.whyItIsWorthRecording: At turn 1 I specifically credited that citation, because the entry named 21f0945 — the genuine D-058 adoption — rather than 4dedc17, the commit that duplicated the register entry and was later dropped at 1b94ad5. That precision is what made the claim checkable, and it was removed during a repair aimed at something else. Restoring the commit costs seven characters. I note it rather than grade it because a plausible reason exists: after the duplicate-and-revert sequence, pinning a single 'the' adoption commit is less clean than it was.

substantiveReviewOfTheBytesIRead.result: No MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX in the content. The claimed repair landed and every other attack fails.
findings: C2-D059-01 is repaired. The COORD row now reads 658c4d1501c9bf6065a2020e33498ae40e18e86c2f9b467d1f2171e20fe0a1c2, which I verified against live bytes, and the entry explains the provenance correctly: 'COORD re-measured to live 658c4d15… after 1b94ad5 dropped the duplicate D-058 entry.' The erroneous 6f5557df pin, which fixed the transient duplicated-register state, is gone.

My turn-1 verdict is pinned at 4b6418d2a75c6d391ca98f00b043fd8c1d46a8dc967708b492823ede66eb8f04, which matches my file, and characterized as 'Claude 2 SHOULD-FIX C2-D059-01' — exactly what I returned, at 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX with that single id. The Codex turn-1 verdict digest d3d22920… also matches its file, confirmed by hashing without opening.
All six other cited digests match live bytes: the D-054 user amendment, the DR-004 v2 disposition, both v2 verdicts, and file 08.
All four cited commits resolve at full hash to the expected decisions: 29670ed… D-054, 33597e8… D-057, aa75926… D-047/D-048, 88764fa… D-049/D-050.

The attack 'D-057 pin list incomplete' fails: the diff from turn 1 touched only the header, the provenance paragraph, the COORD row and the two new turn-1 verdict rows. The Authority and dependency pins section, the Route A remainder, and all six decision clauses are unchanged from the bytes I verified at turn 1, where I established the pin list complete and the Route A remainder an exact three-item match against the disposition's own whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA.

The attacks 'silent SATISFIED', 'treats section31 v4 as the Phase-1A packet', 'file 08 edited' and 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' all fail on those unchanged clauses: the header and clause 3 refuse SATISFIED, clause 3 states 'section31 v4 stays the binding instrument, not the packet' and 'Conditions 2–5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization', clause 4 refuses to edit file 08, file 08 measures unchanged, and git reports zero modified tracked files.
The live register state supports the entry's sibling claim: COORD contains exactly one '## D-058' heading, so the duplicate is gone and D-058 stands adopted once for DR-002.

whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex reviews of D-059 at either turn. Not read; the turn-1 verdict was hashed without opening and the turn-2 file is absent at review time. The entry characterizes Codex turn 1 as 'CONSENT, 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX, 1 NOTE'; I verified the digest and not the class, counts or note.
The current bytes at 28719de6. I did not review them, and this verdict does not extend to them. I do not know how they differ from the bytes I read.
The current prompt at 12a5c44d. The instructions I followed are the ones at 1919f0af, which I measured at start.
The Codex verdict on the DR-004 v2 disposition. Its digest verifies but I did not open it, so the dual half of D-057's dual-ACCEPT precondition rests on the entry's recital of 'ACCEPT 0/0'.
Whether the five-entry D-059-063 draft, whose D-059 records DR-002 rather than DR-004, is withdrawn. Still unstated across files.

environment.note: Both the subject and the review prompt are untracked working-tree files and both moved after my start measurement. My verdict binds 4a28b6fc, the bytes I read.
environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256 of subject and prompt three times at start and four times at end, spaced a second apart, to distinguish stable divergence from a mid-write file; ls and wc for size, mtime and line count; git status to establish the divergence was not mine; difflib line diff and a python3 token-loss pass of the turn-1 bytes against the reviewed turn-2 bytes with every lost token traced; digest verification of all cited inputs against live bytes; git log --format=%s at full hash for each cited commit; heading count for '## D-058' in live COORD

nonConsentNote: I do not CONSENT, on one MUST-FIX, and it is procedural rather than substantive. The repair I asked for landed cleanly — COORD is re-measured to the live 658c4d15 and the erroneous pin to the reverted duplicate state is gone — and on the bytes I read every other attack fails, with all eight digests and four commits verifying. But the dispatch froze the subject at 4a28b6fc and said to object if it moves, and it moved while I was reviewing it, as did the prompt. A verdict has to bind bytes someone else can re-derive, and right now the dispatch, the file and this review disagree about which bytes those are. Re-dispatch at the true digest, hold it, and on this content I expect to consent.
